title: Recipe
description: What becomes what. The only entity type here that is a relation rather than a thing, and it is still a noun: a recipe is a stated fact about the world, where the *doing* of it belongs to the game. Canon says reed fibre and a comb make cordage; whether a particular player has four of the one and one of the other is not canon's business.

process.description: How it is done. The process carries where it must happen and what the maker must be holding, so a recipe never restates a kiln.

tag.description: Any material carrying this class satisfies the ingredient. **The reason this layer is maintainable**: a recipe naming `#fibre` accepts a reed canon has not written yet, where a recipe naming four species has to be edited every time the bestiary grows. Hash-prefixed so a tag is never mistaken for an id. Pinned against material_classes.json by lint.

material.description: This exact material and no substitute. Use where the specific stuff is the point -- pitch, not any resin.

item.description: A made object as an input. Usually a tool, in which case set `kept`.

kept.description: True for a tool: needed to do the work and still there afterwards. Absent means consumed. Getting this wrong is how a recipe layer quietly eats every knife in the world.

outputs.description: A recipe may output a material as well as an item -- pressing gives oil, smelting gives metal. That is what keeps the chain going rather than bottoming out at the first made object.

known_by.description: Culture ids from database/cultures.json that hold this knowledge. Absent means everybody. Checked by lint against that file, the way `culture` on a character is.

epochs.description: Epoch ids. Absent means every epoch. Date anything involving metal.

taught_by.description: `npc_` ids who can show a traveller how. **A recipe with this field must be learned; a recipe without it is common knowledge and is known from the first step.** That rule is the whole of the gating, and it is stated this way round on purpose: 72 recipes offered at once is a wall, and re-authoring all 72 to say `common: true` to fix it would be a worse wall. Silence keeps meaning what it has always meant here -- canon has not said otherwise.
